ocean-acidification-s2.title: How dissolved CO₂ lowers ocean pH

options: The fall in ocean pH as seawater absorbs CO₂
The rise in ocean temperature from trapped heat
The buildup of nitrates from fertilizer runoff
Acid rain falling on lakes and streams

why.correct: The ocean absorbs about a quarter of the CO₂ people release; as it dissolves, it lowers the pH of seawater.
options: Right: dissolved CO₂ forms carbonic acid, raising hydrogen ions and lowering pH.
That is ocean warming, a related but separate change.
Nitrate runoff causes eutrophication, not acidification.
Acid rain comes from SO₂ and NOx; ocean acidification comes from CO₂ in the air.

items.q: When CO₂ dissolves in seawater, which product makes the water more acidic?
options: Oxygen gas released by the reaction
Hydrogen ions from carbonic acid
Calcium carbonate dissolving out of the water
Nitrogen gas from the air

why.correct: pH measures hydrogen ions: more H⁺ means lower pH and more acidic water.
options: The reaction does not release oxygen.
Right: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃, which releases H⁺. More H⁺ means lower pH.
Calcium carbonate is what shells are made of; acidification makes it harder to build.
Nitrogen is not part of the reaction.

items.q: Why does ocean acidification make it harder for corals, clams and some plankton to build shells and skeletons?
options: Acid water is too cold for shells to form
Dissolved CO₂ blocks sunlight from reaching the reef
Hydrogen ions bind carbonate, the shell material
Acid water has too much carbonate for shells to use

why.correct: Fewer carbonate ions mean shell-builders spend more energy making calcium carbonate, and existing shells can start to dissolve.
options: Acidification is a chemical change, not a temperature change.
CO₂ in water does not block light.
Right: H⁺ + CO₃²⁻ → HCO₃⁻ removes the carbonate these animals need.
It has less carbonate, not more.

items.q: Surface ocean pH has fallen from about 8.2 to about 8.1 since the 1700s. Which statement is correct?
options: Seawater is now an acid, with a pH below 7
The change is too small to matter, since pH barely moved
Seawater has become neutral, with a pH of 7
Seawater is still basic, but it is less basic than before

why.correct: Acidification describes a direction: pH falling toward 7, not that the ocean is acidic.
options: A pH of 8.1 is above 7, so it is still basic.
The pH scale is logarithmic, so 0.1 is about 26% more hydrogen ions.
8.1 is not 7.
Right: pH above 7 is basic; "acidification" means moving toward acid.

items.q: Describe the relationship between atmospheric CO₂ and seawater pH in the table.
options: As CO₂ rose, pH fell
As CO₂ rose, pH rose
CO₂ and pH both stayed the same
pH fell until 2005, then rose

why.correct: An inverse relationship: more CO₂ in the air, more CO₂ dissolved, more carbonic acid, lower pH.
options: Right: CO₂ went from 354 to 414 ppm while pH fell from 8.110 to 8.053.
pH fell in every five-year step.
Both changed in every step.
pH kept falling through 2020.

items.q: By how much did the seawater pH change from 1990 to 2020? Give the change as later minus earlier.

mistakes.why: Subtract earlier from later: 8.053 − 8.110. pH fell, so the change is negative.
That is a percent change. The question asks for the change in pH units: 8.053 − 8.110.

items.q: Write the setup for the percent change in atmospheric CO₂ from 1990 to 2020 in the table, then the answer.

mistakes.why: Divide by the old value, 354 ppm in 1990, not the new value.
Without brackets the division happens first. Write (414 − 354) ÷ 354 × 100.
60 ppm is the change in CO₂. Divide by 354 and multiply by 100 for the percent: about 16.9%.

items.q: The pH scale is logarithmic: hydrogen ion concentration multiplies by 10 for each drop of 1 pH unit, so it multiplies by 10 raised to the drop. Using the table, by what factor did hydrogen ion concentration increase from 1990 to 2020?

why.correct: $10^{(8.110 - 8.053)} = 10^{0.057} \approx 1.14$: about 14% more hydrogen ions in 30 years.

mistakes.why: 0.057 is the drop in pH, not the factor. Raise 10 to that power: 10^0.057.
Multiply by 10 for each whole unit means 10 raised to the drop, not 10 times the drop: 10^0.057.

items.q: In the figure, what does CO₂ form when it dissolves in water?
options: Carbonic acid (H₂CO₃)
Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)
Ozone (O₃)
Sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)

why.correct: Dissolved CO₂ reacts with water to form carbonic acid, a weak acid.
options: Right: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃.
Calcium carbonate is the shell material, not the first product.
Ozone is not part of this reaction.
Sulfuric acid comes from SO₂ in acid rain.

items.q: According to the figure, why does adding H⁺ reduce the carbonate ions in seawater?
options: H⁺ turns carbonate into CO₂ gas, which escapes
H⁺ combines with CO₃²⁻ to form HCO₃⁻
H⁺ freezes carbonate into sea ice
H⁺ makes carbonate sink to the deep ocean

why.correct: Fewer carbonate ions remain for animals that build calcium carbonate.
options: In the figure, H⁺ and carbonate form bicarbonate, not CO₂ gas.
Right: each hydrogen ion that grabs a carbonate ion turns it into bicarbonate.
Freezing is not part of the chemistry.
The carbonate is converted, not moved.

items.q: Based on the figure’s pH scale, about how many times more hydrogen ions would surface seawater have at pH 7.8 than at pH 8.1?
options: About 0.3 times
About 3 times
About 2 times
About 30 times
0.3 is the drop in pH, not the factor.
Each whole unit is ten times; 0.3 units is about 2 times, not 3.
Right: a drop of 0.3 pH units is $10^{0.3} \approx 2$ times the hydrogen ions.
That would be a drop of about 1.5 pH units.

items.q: Explain how burning fossil fuels harms oysters and other shell-building animals.

why.correct: Every link: CO₂, carbonic acid, more H⁺, lower pH, less carbonate, weaker shells.

specific.frame: More CO₂ dissolves in seawater and forms ___, so pH ___ and carbonate ions ___, making it harder to build ___.

acid.label: What forms
options: carbonic acid
sulfuric acid
nitric acid

why.1: Sulfuric acid forms from SO₂ in acid rain, not from CO₂.
why.2: Nitric acid forms from NOx, not from CO₂.

ph.label: pH
options: decreases
increases

co3.label: Carbonate ions
options: decrease
increase

why.1: H⁺ combines with carbonate, so carbonate falls.

shell.label: What is harder to build
options: calcium carbonate shells
cell membranes
muscle tissue

why.1: The chemistry affects carbonate, the shell material.
why.2: Muscle tissue is not made of carbonate.

specific.model: Burning fossil fuels adds CO₂ to the air; more CO₂ dissolves in seawater and forms carbonic acid, so pH decreases and carbonate ions decrease because hydrogen ions bind them, making it harder for oysters to build calcium carbonate shells.

items.q: Which organisms are most directly threatened by ocean acidification? Select all that apply.
options: Reef-building corals
Oysters and clams
Kelp, a large brown alga
Sea turtles

why.correct: Animals that make calcium carbonate shells or skeletons, including some plankton at the base of food webs, are hit first.
options: Right: coral skeletons are calcium carbonate.
Right: their shells are calcium carbonate.
Kelp does not build a carbonate shell; some algae may even grow faster with more CO₂.
A sea turtle shell is bone covered with keratin, not calcium carbonate built from seawater, so turtles are not hit first.

items.q: Which action would do the most to slow ocean acidification worldwide?
options: Adding fertilizer to the open ocean
Cutting CO₂ emissions from burning fossil fuels
Phasing out CFCs
Banning sulfur in gasoline

why.correct: Acidification is driven by CO₂ itself, so the global fix is cutting CO₂ emissions.
options: Fertilizer causes algal blooms and dead zones.
Right: less CO₂ in the air means less dissolving into the ocean.
CFCs destroy ozone; they are not the cause of acidification.
That reduces acid rain, not ocean acidification.

items.q: Why does ocean acidification track the Keeling curve so closely?
options: Warmer air directly lowers seawater pH
The Keeling curve measures ocean pH
The ocean absorbs part of the CO₂ added to the air
Acid rain carries CO₂ into the sea

why.correct: The surface ocean and the air exchange CO₂, so ocean chemistry follows the atmosphere.
options: Temperature affects how much CO₂ dissolves, but the cause is the CO₂ itself.
The Keeling curve measures CO₂ in the air.
Right: as CO₂ in the air rises, more dissolves at the surface.
Acid rain is mostly SO₂ and NOx; CO₂ dissolves directly from the air.
